When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, all the people would rise and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.
Yahweh would speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend. When Moses returned to the camp, his young assistant, Joshua son of Nun,{c} would not leave the tent.

Moses said to Yahweh, “See, you say to me, ‘Bring up this people,’ but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.’
Now, if I have found favor in your eyes, show me now your ways, that I may know you and find favor in your eyes. And consider that this nation is your people.”
He said, “My presence{d} will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
He said to him, “If your presence does not go with us, do not carry us up from here.

For how shall it be known that I and your people have found favor in your eyes? Is it not by your going with us, so that we, I and your people, are set apart from all the peoples on the face of the earth?”
Yahweh said to Moses, “I will do this very thing also that you have spoken, for you have found favor in my eyes, and I know you by name.”
Moses said, “Please show me your glory.”

And he said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name Yahweh before you.{e} I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy.”{f}
But he said, “You cannot see my face, for no human being may see me and live.”
Yahweh said, “See, there is a place beside me, where you shall stand upon the rock;
While my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take away my hand, and you will see my back,{g} but my face must not be seen.”

notes.text: Here the “tent of meeting” is a tent pitched outside the camp before the tabernacle was built (compare chapters 35–40).
Hebrew “he.”
Joshua is called “son of Nun” here for the first time. Nun means “fish.”
Hebrew “my face,” so also in verse 15 (“your face”). The Septuagint reads “I myself will go before you.”
Or “I will proclaim my name, ‘Yahweh,’ before you.” See 34:5–7.
Paul quotes these words in Romans 9:15.
Or “my aftermath,” what remains after I have passed. The Hebrew is unusual and the language is deliberately reserved.

verses.text: Yahweh said to Moses, “Cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
Be ready by morning, and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and present yourself there to me on the top of the mountain.
No one shall come up with you, nor let anyone be seen anywhere on the mountain; neither let the flocks or herds feed in front of that mountain.”
So Moses cut two tablets of stone like the first ones. He rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as Yahweh had commanded him, and took in his hand the two tablets of stone.
Yahweh came down in the cloud and stood with him there, and he proclaimed the name Yahweh.{a}
Yahweh passed before him and proclaimed, “Yahweh, Yahweh,{b} a God compassionate and gracious,{c} slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love{d} and faithfulness,{e}

keeping steadfast love for thousands,{f} forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin; yet who will by no means acquit the guilty, but visits the iniquity of fathers on children, and on grandchildren, to the third and the fourth generation.”
Moses quickly bowed his head toward the ground and worshiped.
He said, “If now I have found favor in your sight, Lord,{g} please let the Lord go in our midst, for it is a stiff-necked people. Pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for your inheritance.”

And he said, “See, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will do marvels, such as have never been wrought in all the earth or among any nation; and all the people in whose midst you are shall see the work of Yahweh, for it is an awesome thing that I will do with you.
Keep what I command you today. Look, I am driving out before you the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land to which you are going, or it will become a snare among you.
But you shall demolish their altars, smash their pillars, and cut down their Asherim.{h}
For you are not to bow down to any other god, for Yahweh, whose name is Jealous,{i} is a jealous God.
Take care that you make no covenant with the inhabitants of the land, lest they play the harlot after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, and someone invite you, and you eat of his sacrifice,
and you will take some of their daughters for your sons, and their daughters will prostitute themselves after their gods and make your sons prostitute themselves after their gods.
You are not to make for yourselves gods of cast metal.

“You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you are to eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib (March–April),{j} for in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
Every firstborn{k} belongs to me, all your male livestock, the firstborn of cattle and sheep.
The firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; and if you do not redeem it, then you shall break its neck. All the firstborn of your sons you shall redeem. None shall appear before me empty.
“Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest; in plowing time and in harvest you shall rest.
And you shall keep the Feast of Weeks,{l} the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the year’s end.
Three times in the year all your males are to appear before the Lord Yahweh, the God of Israel.{m}
For I will cast out nations before you and widen your borders; neither shall any man desire your land when you go up three times in the year to appear before Yahweh your God.
“You are not to offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened, and the sacrifice of the Feast of the Passover is not to be left until the morning.
The best of the firstfruits of your ground you are to bring to the house of Yahweh your God. You are not to boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.”{n}
Yahweh said to Moses, “Write these words, for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”
So he was there with Yahweh forty days and forty nights. He neither ate bread nor drank water. And he{o} wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Words.{p}

When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the testimony being in Moses’ hand as he came down from the mountain, Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone{q} because he had spoken with him.{r}
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses talked with them.
Afterward all the Israelites came near, and he commanded them all that Yahweh had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
Whenever Moses went in before Yahweh to speak with him, he would remove the veil until he came out. And when he came out and told the Israelites what he had been commanded,
the Israelites saw that the skin of Moses’ face shone; and Moses would put the veil on his face again, until he went in to speak with him.

notes.text: Or “he called on the name of Yahweh.” The subject may be Yahweh or Moses.

These words (verses 6–7) are Yahweh’s own declaration of his character, the fullest self-description in the Old Testament. They are echoed again and again: Numbers 14:18; Nehemiah 9:17; Psalms 86:15; 103:8; 145:8; Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2; Nahum 1:3. Grammatically the first words may also be read, “Yahweh, Yahweh is a God compassionate….”
Hebrew el rahum vehannun. Rahum, “compassionate,” is related to rehem, “womb,” suggesting a mother’s tender love; hannun, “gracious,” describes favor freely given.
Hebrew hesed, the loyal, committed love that keeps covenant. See the note at 15:13.
Hebrew emet, “truth,” “reliability,” “faithfulness.”
Or “to the thousandth generation” (compare Deuteronomy 7:9). The contrast with “the third and the fourth generation” stresses that God’s mercy far outweighs his judgment.
Hebrew Adonai, “my Lord.” Some Hebrew manuscripts read “Yahweh.”
Hebrew asherim, wooden poles or images associated with the goddess Asherah.
Hebrew Qanna. On God’s jealousy, see the note at 20:5. Here “Jealous” is presented as a name, expressing his exclusive claim on his people.
Hebrew “the month of Abib.” See the note at 13:4.
Hebrew “everything that opens the womb.”
Hebrew shavu‘ot, later called Pentecost (“fiftieth”), because it came seven weeks (fifty days) after Passover.
Hebrew ha’adon YHWH elohe yisra’el, “the Lord Yahweh, the God of Israel.” On ha’adon see the note at 23:17.
See the note at 23:19.
The context suggests that Yahweh is the one who wrote (verse 1; Deuteronomy 10:2–4), though grammatically the subject could be Moses (verse 27).
Hebrew “the ten words,” the source of the term “Decalogue.” Compare Deuteronomy 4:13; 10:4.

Hebrew qaran, related to qeren, “horn.” The verb probably means “sent out rays.” The Latin Vulgate rendered it cornuta, “horned,” which led to medieval and Renaissance art (including Michelangelo’s statue) showing Moses with horns. The Septuagint reads “was glorified.” Compare 2 Corinthians 3:7–18.
That is, with Yahweh.

verses.text: Moses gathered all the assembly of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things which Yahweh has commanded you to do:{a}
For six days work shall be done, but the seventh day shall be holy to you, a Sabbath of complete rest to Yahweh; whoever works on that day shall be put to death.
You shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations on the Sabbath day.”
And Moses spoke to all the assembly of the Israelites, saying, “This is what Yahweh has commanded:
Take from among you an offering for Yahweh. Whoever has a willing heart, let him bring it as Yahweh’s offering: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and stones to be set, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
“Let every skilled person among you come and make all that Yahweh has commanded:
the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps and its frames, its crossbars, its posts, and its bases;
the ark and its poles, the atonement cover, and the veil of the screen;
the table and its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand also for the light, with its utensils, its lamps, and the oil for the light;
the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil, the sweet incense, and the hanging for the door at the entrance of the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt offering with its grating of bronze, its poles, and all its utensils, the basin and its stand;
the hangings of the court, with its pillars and its sockets, and the hanging for the gate of the court;
the tent pegs of the tabernacle and the tent pegs of the courtyard, and their cords;
the finely woven garments for ministering in the Holy Place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, for their service as priests.”
Then all the congregation of the Israelites departed from the presence of Moses.

And they came, everyone whose heart stirred him, and everyone whose spirit moved him, and brought Yahweh’s offering for the work of the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.

They came, both men and women, all who had a willing heart, and brought brooches, earrings, signet rings, and necklaces,{b} all sorts of gold objects, everyone presenting an offering of gold to Yahweh.
Every man with whom was found blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, or fine leather, or rams’ skins dyed red, brought it.
Everyone who could make an offering of silver or bronze brought it as Yahweh’s offering, and everyone who had acacia wood for any work of the service brought it.
All the women who were wise of heart spun with their hands, and brought what they had spun: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts stirred them with skill spun the goats’ hair.
The leaders brought onyx stones and stones to be set, for the ephod and for the breastpiece,
and the spices and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
All the men and women of the Israelites whose heart moved them to bring anything for all the work that Yahweh had commanded through Moses to be done brought it as a freewill offering to Yahweh.
Then Moses said to the Israelites, “See, Yahweh has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
and he has filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all kinds of workmanship,
to devise artistic designs, to work in gold, in silver, and in bronze,
in cutting jewels for setting, in carving wood, for making any kind of skilled work.
And he has put it in his heart to teach, both he and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with wisdom of heart to do every sort of work of the engraver, and of the skilled designer, and of the embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and in fine linen, and of the weaver—they do every work, and they devise skillful designs.

notes.text: Chapters 35–40 report how the instructions of chapters 25–31 were carried out, repeating them almost word for word. In the Septuagint these chapters are shorter and arranged in a different order: for example, the priestly garments (Hebrew 39) come before the tabernacle structure (Hebrew 36), the making of the incense altar (Hebrew 37:25–28) is not reported, and several sections are abbreviated. In Brenton’s English edition the chapters are numbered differently, so that the curtains appear in chapter 37 and the ark in chapter 38. Scholars debate whether the Greek translator abridged and rearranged the Hebrew or worked from a different Hebrew edition. This translation follows the Hebrew order.
Or “pendants.” The identity of some of these ornaments is uncertain.

verses.text: “Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person in whom Yahweh has put skill and understanding to know how to do all the work for the service of the sanctuary are to work according to all that Yahweh has commanded.”
Then Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every wise-hearted man in whose heart Yahweh had put wisdom, everyone whose heart was stirred up to come to the work to do it.
They received from Moses all the offering that the Israelites had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, to make it. They kept bringing him freewill offerings every morning,
so all the wise men who were doing every work of the sanctuary came, each from his own work which he was doing,
and said to Moses, “The people are bringing much more than enough for the service of the work that Yahweh has commanded us to do.”
So Moses gave a command, and they proclaimed throughout the camp: “Neither man nor woman is to make any further work for the offering of the sanctuary.” Thus the people were restrained from bringing.
for the material they had was sufficient for all the work to be done, and more than enough.

Every wise-hearted man among those who did the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; with cherubim, the work of a skilled designer, he made them.
The length of each curtain was about 42 feet, and the width of each curtain about 6 feet;{a} all the curtains had the same measurements.
He{b} joined five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he joined to one another.
And he made loops of blue on the edge of one curtain at the end of the first set; so also he made them on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.
He made fifty loops on the one curtain, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that was in the second set. The loops were opposite one another.
And he made fifty hooks of gold and coupled the curtains to one another with the hooks, so that it became one tabernacle.
He also made curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the tabernacle; he made eleven curtains.
The length of each curtain was about 45 feet, and the width of each curtain about 6 feet;{c} the eleven curtains had the same measurements.
He joined five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves.
And he made fifty loops on the edge of the last curtain of the first set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
He made fifty clasps of bronze to join the tent together, so that it might be a single whole.
He made for the tent a covering of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above that.
He made the upright frames for the tabernacle of acacia wood.
The length of a frame was about 15 feet, and the width of each frame about 2¼ feet.{d}
Each frame had two tenons for joining them together. He did this for all the frames of the tabernacle.
He made the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side.
And forty sockets of silver he made under the twenty boards: two sockets under the one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under the next board for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, he made twenty frames
and their forty sockets of silver: two sockets under the one board, and two sockets under the next board.
And for the rear of the tabernacle toward the west he made six boards.
He made two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They were doubled at the bottom and likewise complete at the top, up to the first ring. He made both of them this way for the two corners.
So there were eight boards, and their sockets were of silver, sixteen sockets—under each board two sockets.
And he made bars of acacia wood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle at the rear toward the west.
He made the middle crossbar to run halfway up the frames from end to end.
He overlaid the frames with gold and made their rings of gold as holders for the crossbars, and he overlaid the crossbars with gold.
He made the veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen; with cherubim, skillfully worked, he made it.
He made four posts of acacia for it and overlaid them with gold. Their hooks were of gold, and he cast for them four bases of silver.
He also made a hanging for the door of the tent, embroidered with needlework, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen,
and its five posts with their hooks. He overlaid their tops and their bands with gold, and their five bases were of bronze.

notes.text: Hebrew “twenty-eight cubits” and “four cubits,” about 12.6 by 1.8 meters. A cubit was about 18 inches (45 centimeters); see the note at 25:10.
That is, Bezalel (37:1), with those who worked under him.
Hebrew “thirty cubits” and “four cubits,” about 13.5 by 1.8 meters.
Hebrew “ten cubits” and “a cubit and a half,” about 4.5 by 0.7 meters.

verses.text: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood, about 3¾ feet long, 2¼ feet wide, and 2¼ feet high.{a}
He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold around it.
He cast for it four rings of gold for its four feet, two rings on one side of it and two rings on the other side.
He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold,
and put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark.
He made an atonement cover of pure gold, about 3¾ feet long and 2¼ feet wide.{b}
He made two cherubim of gold; he made them of hammered work at the two ends of the atonement cover,
one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end. He made the cherubim of one piece with the atonement cover at its two ends.
The cherubim spread out their wings above, overshadowing the atonement cover with their wings, with their faces toward one another; the faces of the cherubim were toward the atonement cover.
He made the table of acacia wood, about 3 feet long, 1½ feet wide, and 2¼ feet high.{c}
He overlaid it with pure gold and made a molding of gold around it.
He made a rim around it about 3 inches wide,{d} and made a molding of gold around the rim.
He cast four rings of gold for it and fastened the rings at the four corners at its four legs.
Close to the rim were the rings, as places for the poles to carry the table.
And he made the poles of acacia wood for carrying the table, and overlaid them with gold.
He made the utensils that were on the table, its plates and its dishes, its bowls and its jars for pouring out drink offerings, of pure gold.
He made the lampstand of pure gold, making it of hammered work; its base and its stem, its cups, its knobs, and its flowers were of one piece with it.
Six branches went out from its sides, three branches of the lampstand from one side of it and three branches of the lampstand from the other side of it.

There were three cups shaped like almond blossoms on one branch, each with a knob and a flower, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the next branch, each with a knob and a flower; so for the six branches going out from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their knobs and flowers,

and a knob under the first pair of branches, of one piece with it, and a knob under the second pair of branches, of one piece with it, and a knob under the third pair of branches, of one piece with it, for the six branches going out from it.
Their knobs and their branches were of one piece with it; all of it was one hammered piece of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, its snuffers, and its trays of pure gold.
He made it and all its utensils from about 75 pounds of pure gold.{e}
He made the altar of incense of acacia wood. It was about 18 inches long and 18 inches wide, square, and about 3 feet high.{f} Its horns were of one piece with it.
He overlaid it with pure gold, its top, its sides all around, and its horns, and he made a molding of gold around it.
And he made two gold rings for it below its molding, on opposite sides of it, as places for the poles with which to carry it.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
He made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.

notes.text: Hebrew “two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high,” about 1.1 by 0.7 by 0.7 meters. A cubit was about 18 inches (45 centimeters); see the note at 25:10.
Hebrew “two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide,” about 1.1 by 0.7 meters.
Hebrew “two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high,” about 90 by 45 by 70 centimeters.
Hebrew “a handbreadth,” about 3 inches (7.5 centimeters).
Hebrew “a talent of pure gold,” about 75 pounds (34 kilograms).
Hebrew “a cubit long and a cubit wide … two cubits high,” about 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high.

verses.text: He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood, about 7½ feet long and 7½ feet wide. It was square, and about 4½ feet high.{a}
He made its horns on its four corners; its horns were of one piece with it, and he overlaid it with bronze.
He made all the utensils of the altar, the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the firepans; he made all its utensils of bronze.
And he made for the altar a grating of bronze network, beneath its ledge, reaching halfway up.
He cast four rings for the four corners of the bronze grating, to be places for the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, with which to carry it; he made it hollow, with planks.
He made the laver of bronze, with its base of bronze, from the bronze mirrors{b} of the women who ministered{c} at the door of the tent of meeting.
Then he made the court. On the south side, toward the south, the hangings of the court were of fine twisted linen, about 150 feet in length;{d}
with their twenty posts and their twenty bases of bronze; the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
For the north side there were hangings about 150 feet long, with their twenty posts and their twenty bases of bronze; the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
For the west side there were hangings about 75 feet long,{e} with their ten posts and their ten bases; the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
For the front, to the east, about 75 feet.
The hangings for one side of the entrance were about 22½ feet long,{f} with their three posts and their three bases.
So also for the other side; on both sides of the gate of the courtyard were hangings about 22½ feet long, with their three posts and their three bases.
All the hangings around the courtyard were of fine twisted linen.
The bases for the posts were of bronze, the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver, and the overlaying of their tops was of silver. All the posts of the courtyard were banded with silver.

The hanging for the gate of the court was of embroidered work, in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen; about 30 feet in length,{g} and in height about 7½ feet,{h} corresponding to the hangings of the court.
Their pillars were four, with their four sockets of bronze; their hooks were of silver, and the overlay of their tops and their bands were of silver.
And all the pegs for the tabernacle and for the court round about were of bronze.

These are the records{i} of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, as they were recorded at the command of Moses, the work of the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.{j}
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that Yahweh commanded Moses.
And with him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman and designer, and an embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
All the gold that was used for the work, in all the work of the sanctuary, the gold of the offering, came to about 2,200 pounds, by the sanctuary standard.{k}
The silver from those of the congregation who were counted came to about 7,500 pounds, by the sanctuary standard:{l}
a fifth of an ounce a head,{m} that is, half the sanctuary standard, for everyone who passed over to those who were counted, from twenty years old and upward, for 603,550 men.
The 7,500 pounds{n} of silver were used for casting the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil: a hundred bases from it, about 75 pounds for each base.
From the remaining silver, about 44 pounds,{o} he made hooks for the posts, overlaid their tops, and made bands for them.
The bronze of the offering came to about 5,300 pounds.{p}
With it he made the sockets at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the bronze altar with its bronze grating, and all the utensils for the altar,
and the sockets of the court round about, and the sockets at the court gate, with all the pegs of the tabernacle, and all the pegs of the court round about.

notes.text: Hebrew “five cubits long and five cubits wide … three cubits high,” about 2.3 meters square and 1.4 meters high.
Ancient mirrors were made of polished bronze.

Hebrew tsava’, used of organized service, including Levitical service at the sanctuary (Numbers 4:23; 8:24). Compare 1 Samuel 2:22. The nature of these women’s service is not explained. The Septuagint reads “of the women who fasted.”
Hebrew “a hundred cubits,” about 45 meters. So also in verse 11.
Hebrew “fifty cubits,” about 23 meters. So also in verse 13.
Hebrew “fifteen cubits,” about 6.8 meters. So also in verse 15.
Hebrew “twenty cubits,” about 9 meters.

Or “the inventory.”
Verses 21–31 are an accounting of the materials. In the Septuagint, this material appears in a different place and form (see the note at 35:1).

Hebrew “twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels,” about 1,000 kilograms. A talent was about 75 pounds (34 kilograms) and a shekel about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams); a talent was 3,000 shekels. Standards varied, so these figures are approximate. On the “sanctuary standard” (Hebrew “shekel of the sanctuary”), see the note at 30:13. Some Septuagint manuscripts read 720 shekels.
Hebrew “a hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels,” about 3,400 kilograms.

verses.text: From the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn they made finely woven garments for ministering in the Holy Place. They made the holy garments for Aaron, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen.
And they beat the gold into thin sheets and cut it into threads, to work it into the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and the fine linen, with skillful design.
They made shoulder pieces for it, joined to it at its two edges, so that it was joined together.
And the skillfully woven band that was upon it was of the same piece and workmanship—of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen—as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
They prepared the onyx stones, set in settings of gold filigree, engraved as a seal is engraved, with the names of the sons of Israel.
And he set them on the shoulder straps of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He made the breastpiece, the work of a skilled designer, in the same style as the ephod, of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen.
It was square. They made the breastpiece folded double, about 9 inches long and about 9 inches wide when folded.{a}
They set in it four rows of stones. A row of carnelian, topaz, and emerald was the first row;{b}
the second row a turquoise, a lapis lazuli, and a diamond;
the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. They were enclosed in settings of gold filigree.
And the stones were twelve, according to the names of the sons of Israel; each was engraved like a signet with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
And they made chains on the breastplate like cords, of braided work of pure gold.
They made two settings of gold filigree and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastpiece.
And they put the two braided chains of gold in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate.
The other two ends of the two cords they attached to the two settings, and so attached them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
And they made two rings of gold and put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on its edge, which was on the inside toward the ephod.
They made two rings of gold and attached them to the two shoulder straps of the ephod, at the lower part, in front, close to its seam, above the skillfully woven band of the ephod.

And they tied the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it might lie above the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and not come loose from the ephod, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He made the robe of the ephod, woven work, all of blue.
In the middle of the robe was the opening, like the opening of a coat of mail,{c} with a binding all around the opening, so that it would not tear.
On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and twisted linen.
They made bells of pure gold and set the bells between the pomegranates all around the hem of the robe, among the pomegranates:
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, around the hem of the robe for ministering, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
They made the tunics of fine linen, woven work, for Aaron and his sons,
and the turban of fine linen, the ornamental headbands of fine linen, the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen,
and the sash of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, the work of an embroiderer, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold and wrote on it an inscription, like the engraving of a seal, “Holy to Yahweh.”
And they fastened to it a blue cord, to attach it above to the turban, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
So all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was finished. The Israelites did according to all that Yahweh had commanded Moses; so they did.
Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses, the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, its frames, its crossbars, its posts, and its bases;
the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the veil of the screen;
the ark of the testimony with its poles and the atonement cover;
the table with all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the pure lampstand with its lamps, the lamps set in order, and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
the golden altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;
the bronze altar with its grating of bronze, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin and its stand;

the hangings of the court, with its pillars and its sockets, and the hanging for the court gate, its cords and its pegs; and all the instruments for the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
the finely woven garments for ministering in the Holy Place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for their service as priests.
According to all that Yahweh had commanded Moses, so the Israelites had done all the work.
Moses looked over all the work, and behold, they had done it; as Yahweh had commanded, so they had done. And Moses blessed them.{d}

notes.text: Hebrew “a span long and a span wide,” about 23 centimeters square. See the note at 28:16.
On the identification of these stones, see the notes at 28:17–18.
See the note at 28:32.
The completion and blessing echo the end of the creation account: compare Genesis 1:31–2:3.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“On the first day of the first month (in March–April){a} you are to set up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
You are to put the ark of the testimony in it, and screen the ark with the veil.
You are to bring in the table and set out its arrangement. You are to bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
And you shall set the golden altar of incense before the ark of the testimony, and put up the hanging at the door of the tabernacle.
You are to put the altar of burnt offering before the entrance of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting,
and put the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
And you shall set up the court all around, and hang up the hanging at the court gate.
“And you shall take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; and you shall hallow it and all its furniture, and it shall be holy.
And you shall anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and sanctify the altar, and the altar shall be most holy.
You are to anoint the basin and its stand, and consecrate it.
Then you are to bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water,
and put the holy garments on Aaron; and you shall anoint him and sanctify him, that he may minister to me as priest.
You are to bring his sons and put tunics on them,
and anoint them as you anointed their father, so that they may serve me as priests. Their anointing will make them a priesthood forever throughout their generations.”
Moses did this; according to all that Yahweh commanded him, so he did.
In the first month (March–April) of the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was set up.{b}
Moses set up the tabernacle. He laid its bases, set up its frames, put in its crossbars, and raised its posts.
He spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering of the tent over it, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He took the testimony and put it into the ark. He set the poles on the ark and put the atonement cover above on the ark.
And he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the veil of the covering, and screened the ark of the testimony, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He put the table in the tent of meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil,
and arranged the bread on it before Yahweh, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He put the lampstand in the tent of meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle,
and set up the lamps before Yahweh, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He put the golden altar in the tent of meeting before the veil,
and burned sweet incense on it, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He set up the screen at the entrance of the tabernacle.
And he set the altar of burnt offering by the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and offered upon it the burnt offering and the grain offering, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He put the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it for washing.
Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and their feet from it.
Whenever they entered the tent of meeting and drew near the altar, they washed, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
He set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and hung up the screen of the gate of the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle.
Moses was not able to enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud settled{c} on it, and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out on all their journeys.
But if the cloud was not taken up, they would not set out until the day that it was taken up.
For the cloud of Yahweh was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it{d} by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.

notes.text: Hebrew “On the first day of the first month,” that is, Abib or Nisan, the first month of the spring-start religious calendar. See the note at 12:2.

Hebrew “In the first month in the second year, on the first of the month,” that is, the first day of Abib or Nisan (see the note at 12:2), almost a year after the exodus (12:6; 19:1). The Septuagint adds “after they went out of Egypt.”
Hebrew shakan, “to dwell,” the verb from which mishkan, “tabernacle,” comes (see the note at 25:9). Later Jewish tradition spoke of God’s dwelling presence as the Shekhinah.
Or “in the cloud.”
